plan_a_advantages: Potentially lower risk of overtraining due to the extremely low volume of structured training.
Simple and easy to adhere to, requiring minimal planning or effort.
plan_b_advantages: Includes a dedicated aerobic session to build a stronger foundation.
Gradually increases run duration, promoting adaptation and improved endurance.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses almost entirely on very easy runs, which could be beneficial for recovery, it lacks any structured stimulus for improving speed or endurance. Plan B incorporates a dedicated aerobic session and gradually increases the duration of easy runs, providing a more progressive approach to building a stronger aerobic base – a crucial component for trail running speed. The longer, consistent easy runs in Plan B are more likely to translate to improved stamina and efficiency on the trails compared to the repetitive, short easy runs in Plan A.
